# Keep tooltips within screen bounds

## Problem statement

Tooltips are rendered at a fixed offset from the hover point without any viewport-bounds checking. When a hovered element sits near the right or bottom edge of the window, the tooltip overflows the viewport; in the DOM-rendered mode this extends the document's scrollable area, so the page "resizes to make space" (scrollbars appear / layout shifts). The tooltip must always be positioned so that it is fully visible and never alters the document layout.

## Users

- **Players** hovering cards, HUD elements, and buttons in Main Street, Lost Cities, Sushi Go, and the Gym tooltip/Gym-card-index demos.
- **Engine consumers (game developers)** who rely on the shared `TooltipManager` (DOM and Phaser modes) so they do not have to re-implement bounds handling per game.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I hover a card near the right edge of the screen, the tooltip appears fully on-screen instead of being clipped or pushing the page wider.
- As a player, showing a tooltip never causes the game canvas or page to jump/resize.
- As a game developer, when I supply a `phaserRender` callback I can clamp my tooltip into the game canvas with a shared helper rather than copying clamp maths between games.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **DOM-mode clamping:** For a hover point near each of the four viewport edges, the DOM tooltip's rendered bounding rectangle is fully inside the browser viewport (`left >= 0`, `top >= 0`, `right <= window.innerWidth`, `bottom <= window.innerHeight`), with a small margin. Verified by a browser (`*.browser.test.ts`) test in `tests/ui/`.
2. **No document resize:** Showing (and hiding) a DOM tooltip does not change the document scroll size — no horizontal/vertical scrollbar is introduced (`document.documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth` and `scrollHeight === clientHeight` before and after `show()`). Verified by a browser test.
3. **Phaser-mode clamping:** The shared Phaser render callbacks keep their tooltip containers inside the game canvas bounds (`0..GAME_W` × `0..GAME_H`) at all four edges. Gym's callback (currently unclamped) is brought in line with the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, ideally via a shared, unit-tested helper. Verified by unit tests (helper) plus the existing scene/browser tests.
4. **No regression to existing positioning:** Existing world→screen coordinate mapping (canvas scale, canvas offset, camera scroll) and the settings `showTooltips` toggle behaviour are preserved; the existing `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` / `TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` expectations are updated rather than weakened.
5. **Validation and documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (tooltip component section) and any relevant Gym help text. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependencies.
- Must not regress reduced-motion, `pointer-events: none`, or the maximum `z-index` behaviour of the DOM tooltip.
- Must remain safe in non-DOM environments (`document`/`window` undefined) and when the canvas bounding rect cannot be read — fall back to hiding, as today.
- Clamping must be cheap (measure once per `show()`, no per-frame layout thrash, no resize listeners).
- The DOM tooltip node must not contribute to the document's scrollable overflow area.
- Use UK English in comments and docs; escape only backticks in worklog content.
- Existing tests that assert `div.style.position === 'absolute'` will need updating if the positioning strategy changes (see Risks).

## Existing state

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — `TooltipManager`. DOM mode computes `screenX`/`screenY` from the canvas rect, camera scroll, and scale, then sets `left`/`top` = point + `(10, 10)` offset with **no bounds check**. The node is `position: absolute`, `pointer-events: none`, `z-index: 2147483647`, `max-width: 320px`, appended to `document.body`. Phaser mode delegates layout entirely to the caller's `phaserRender` callback.
- Consumers in DOM mode: Main Street (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` constructs it; `MainStreetRendererStreet/Hud/Market/Layout.ts` call `show`), `GymTooltipScene` DOM half, `GymCardIndexScene`.
- Consumers in Phaser mode: `LostCitiesScene.ts` (`createTooltipManager`) and `SushiGoScene.ts` — both already clamp with `Phaser.Math.Clamp(..., 4, GAME_W - boxW - 4)` etc. `GymTooltipScene`'s Phaser callback does **not** clamp.
- Tests: `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` (unit), `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` (browser, asserts `position === 'absolute'`), `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` (SLL anchors only), plus Main Street tooltip content tests.
- Docs: `docs/DEVELOPER.md` documents `TooltipManager`; `docs/gym/GYM_INDEX.md` maps the tooltip scenes.

## Desired change

- Add viewport-bounds clamping to the shared DOM tooltip renderer in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`:
  - Position the node relative to the viewport so it cannot extend the document scroll area (e.g. `position: fixed`).
  - Measure the node after setting content, then flip it above/left of the hover point when there is not enough room below/right, and clamp to the viewport as a final guard, keeping a small margin.
  - Keep the existing world→screen conversion (canvas rect + camera scroll + scale).
- Extract a reusable bounds-clamping helper for in-canvas (Phaser) tooltips, mirroring the Lost Cities / Sushi Go precedent, and use it in `GymTooltipScene` (and optionally migrate Lost Cities / Sushi Go to the shared helper with no behaviour change).
- Add unit tests for the clamp maths (all four edges, both axes, oversized tooltip) and browser tests proving the tooltip stays in the viewport and does not change document scroll size.
- Update `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (and Gym help text if the scene behaviour/description changes).
- **Test-first:** author the clamp-helper unit tests and the browser edge/document-scroll tests before wiring the DOM renderer and the Gym callback, so the new behaviour is specified by failing tests first.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` — Add DOM-mode viewport clamping / anti-resize positioning; export a reusable Phaser-mode clamp helper.
- `example-games/gym/scenes/GymTooltipScene.ts` — Apply the clamp helper in the `phaserRender` callback (currently unclamped).
- `example-games/lost-cities/scenes/LostCitiesScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `example-games/sushi-go/scenes/SushiGoScene.ts` — Optional: migrate duplicated clamp maths to the shared helper (no behaviour change).
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.test.ts` — Unit tests for clamp maths via the DOM mock and helper.
- `tests/ui/TooltipManager.browser.test.ts` — Edge-position + document-scroll-size assertions; update the `position` selector assumption.
- `tests/gym/GymTooltipLayout.test.ts` — Extend with Gym Phaser-mode in-bounds assertions (if the scene callback is changed).
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — Document the bounds guarantee for both tooltip modes.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the correct, complete interpretation of the title is "no tooltip (in either DOM or Phaser mode) may render outside its visible bounds", not just the DOM overlay. The DOM mode is the cause of the reported page-resize; Phaser mode only clips. Recommended and assumed.
- **Assumption:** clamping (shift/flip to stay visible) is preferred over truncating content or shrinking the tooltip. Documented assumption; trivially revisitable.
- **Risk:** switching the DOM node to `position: fixed` invalidates the existing browser test's `position === 'absolute'` selector — update the selector to target the tooltip by its stable attributes (`pointer-events: none` + `z-index`) rather than `position`.
- **Risk:** measuring the node to clamp requires it to be laid out; setting `display: block` before measuring may cause a one-frame flash. Mitigate by measuring immediately after content is set and before paint (single synchronous reflow), or measure with `visibility: hidden` then reveal.
- **Risk:** `window`/`document` may be undefined in unit tests/SSR — guard clamping behind the existing `document` checks and fall back to the unclamped path (or hide) when dimensions are unavailable.
- **Risk:** double clamping when a game's `phaserRender` already clamps — the helper must be opt-in and not re-apply automatically to caller-managed containers.
- **Risk:** oversized tooltips (taller/wider than the viewport) cannot fit; clamp to the margin and accept partial visibility, documenting the behaviour.
- **Scope-creep risk:** tooltip content wrapping/truncation, touch/long-press tooltips, and tooltip theming are out of scope; record as separate work items if raised.

## Related work

- **CG-0MLW74R8B04GYNP7** – Implement tooltip display/hide on card hover (completed) — introduced the shared `TooltipManager` this bug affects.
- **CG-0MODIX70W002JXQN** – `feat(ui): add TooltipManager` / `fix(ui): DOM-positioned tooltip displays above cards` — prior DOM coordinate-mapping work in `src/ui/Tooltip.ts`.
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed) — SLL precedent for declarative positioning.
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed) — SLL layout system; relevant if bounds handling is expressed via SLL zones.
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed) — Main Street tooltip content fix, no overlap with positioning.

### Related work (automated report)

#### Related work items
- **CG-0MP7IZ4RK008065O** – Adapt tutorial system to use layout description (completed)
- **CG-0MP7IVTI50055EXQ** – Screen layout language (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHBHR20095NY8** – Identify and fix Park card tooltip content (completed)

#### Repository file matches
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: ake, bounds, displayed, ensure, keep (+11 more)
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+10 more)
- `AGENTS.md` — matched: ake, bounds, ensure, keep, need (+7 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Q:** Are there open questions requiring producer input? — **A:** No. The seed context ("Sometimes when a tooltip is displayed it would render outside the screen bounds. This results in the screen resizing to make space. We need to ensure that the tooltip is positioned such that it stays within screen bounds.") plus repository research was sufficient to draft a clear, testable brief. No interview round was required. Source: seed context supplied with the intake invocation + repo inspection.

**Prior related answers:** none.

**Research summary:** Inspected `src/ui/Tooltip.ts` (DOM node is `position: absolute` on `document.body` with no bounds check — the resize cause; Phaser mode delegates to `phaserRender`), the four in-repo consumers (Main Street, Gym DOM, Gym Phaser, Lost Cities, Sushi Go), and the existing tests/docs. Lost Cities and Sushi Go already clamp inside the canvas with `Phaser.Math.Clamp`; Gym and the DOM renderer do not. No existing shared clamp helper exists. Related completed tooltip work items were found via `wl search` (see automated report).
data.title: Keep tooltips within screen bounds

## Failure Signature

- Test name: tests/golf/replay.test.ts Replay CLI -- transcript validation
- Failing commit: (not available)
- CI job: (not available)

## Evidence

- Short stderr/stdout excerpt (first 1k characters):

```
AssertionError: expected Error: Could not auto-detect game type (fixture not found at ../../example-games/golf/tests/fixtures/transcripts/fixture-game.json) to contain version
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout `dev` (the failure is reproducible at `a341ec3c`).
2. Run the failing test with **no** `GAMES_CONFIG` override (the documented default unit profile):
   `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts`
   (equivalent: `/skill:test --type unit`)
3. Observe 4 failures in `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (12 passed, 5 skipped):
   - `Replay CLI -- transcript validation > invalid transcript files > should exit with error for wrong transcript version`
   - `Replay CLI -- transcript validation > invalid transcript files > should exit with error for missing initialState`
   - `Replay CLI -- v1 transcript handling > should reject v1 transcript when --stop-at is used`
   - `Replay CLI -- v1 transcript handling > should accept v1 transcript for regular replay (no --stop-at)`
4. Capture full logs and attach to the work item.

## Impact

Failing test detected by agent during automated run. May block PR creation for the agent's current work item.

## Root Cause & Reproduction

`scripts/replay.ts` is core-owned and registers replay adapters from the **active build preset** via `registerConfiguredAdapters(process.cwd())`. The default preset is `core-only` (`scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` → `DEFAULT_PRESET`), which registers **no** adapters. Adapter auto-detection then fails with `Could not auto-detect game type from transcript. Available adapters: none.` (and `--game golf` fails with `Unknown game type 'golf'. Available adapters: none`).

`tests/golf/replay.test.ts` spawns the CLI with `env: { ...process.env }`, so it inherits whatever `GAMES_CONFIG` the runner provides:

- **Red:** a bare `npx vitest run --project unit …` and the project-local `/skill:test --type unit` profile (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`) do **not** export `GAMES_CONFIG`, so the preset is `core-only` and the 4 tests above fail.
- **Green:** `npm test`, `npm run test:smoke` and `npm run test:dev` set `GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"` in their shell runners, so the golf adapter is registered and the tests pass.

A separate **latent** defect was already fixed on `dev` while this plan ran: `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` was `'../../example-games/golf/…'`, resolving one level above the repo root (introduced when the test moved to `tests/golf/` in `fbee2e51`). Corrected to `'example-games/golf/…'` in `a341ec3c`. That fix is necessary but **not sufficient** — under `core-only` the test still fails.

## Chosen Fix (producer-confirmed 2026-09-26)

**Option 1 — test-local, keep the test hermetic.** Export the preset the test needs to the spawned CLI, e.g. in `runReplay()`:

```ts
env: { ...process.env, GAMES_CONFIG: process.env.GAMES_CONFIG ?? 'full' },
```

Rationale: `/skill:test --type unit` is the documented "minimum bar for every change" and `npx vitest run --project unit tests/<game>/` is the documented targeted command, so this file must pass with `GAMES_CONFIG` unset. Forcing `full` only as a fallback preserves an explicitly supplied preset and keeps the core unit profiles runnable under `core-only` — consistent with `tests/scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.test.ts` ("core test profiles must stay runnable even with a bad `GAMES_CONFIG`").

**Rejected (Option 2):** adding `GAMES_CONFIG=full` to the `unit`/`smoke`/`dev` commands in `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`. This is agent infrastructure out of bounds for agents and would not fix a bare `npx vitest run` for a developer.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` passes under the **default unit profile with no `GAMES_CONFIG` override** — `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (and `/skill:test --type unit`) reports 0 failures — while continuing to pass under `GAMES_CONFIG=full` (`npm test`).
2. The test documents (in a code comment) why it pins `GAMES_CONFIG` to the full preset, and the already-corrected `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` path (`example-games/golf/…`) is preserved. Related documentation is updated if any workflow/profile behaviour changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes (`npm test`).

**Key Files:**

- `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` — set the `GAMES_CONFIG` fallback in the spawned CLI env; document the preset dependency; keep the corrected fixture path.
- `scripts/replay.ts` — context only: preset-driven adapter registration (`registerConfiguredAdapters`); no change expected.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — context only: `DEFAULT_PRESET = 'core-only'`; no change expected.

**Note:** the two `scripts/` paths are context only; the fix is confined to the test file.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.

## Suspected Owner

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-09-26 (plan skill): Auto-plan pre-check returned **skip** (Effort Extra Small / Risk Low). During the run another agent closed the item (`completed`, commit `a341ec3c`), which fixed only the latent fixture path. Re-verified `dev` at `a341ec3c`: still 4 failures under the default unit profile; an OPEN QUESTION was recorded and the item was flagged for producer review. Producer answered **reopen** + **Option 1**; item re-claimed `in_progress`, description updated with root cause, chosen fix, refined ACs, Key Files and this changelog. No children created (Extra Small item, auto-complete path); coverage review `proceed`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Questions asked during the plan run

- **Q: The item was closed mid-session but the test still fails under the default `unit` profile — should it be reopened, or should a follow-up be filed?** — **Answer (producer): reopen.** Source: interactive reply 2026-09-26. Evidence: `npx vitest run --project unit tests/golf/replay.test.ts` (GAMES_CONFIG unset) → 4 failed / 12 passed / 5 skipped on `dev` at `a341ec3c`; comment recorded on the work item.
- **Q: Which fix is intended — (1) test-local `GAMES_CONFIG` fallback in `tests/golf/replay.test.ts`, or (2) `GAMES_CONFIG=full` in `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`?** — **Answer (producer): Option 1 (test-local).** Source: interactive reply 2026-09-26. Final: Option 1.

### Research summary

`wl show CG-0MUILDS3200656TU` and the parent `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` established the seed context. Reproduction on `dev` (`a341ec3c`) with `GAMES_CONFIG` unset produced 4 failures; the same file passes with `GAMES_CONFIG=full`. `scripts/replay.ts` → `registerConfiguredAdapters(process.cwd())` and `scripts/adapters/index.ts` showed preset-driven, dynamic adapter registration, with `DEFAULT_PRESET = 'core-only'` in `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts`. `tests/golf/replay.test.ts` spawns the CLI with `env: { ...process.env }`. `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`, `scripts/run-smoke-tests.sh` and `scripts/run-dev-tests.sh` each `export GAMES_CONFIG="${GAMES_CONFIG:-full}"`, whereas `.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`'s typed commands do not. `git show fbee2e51` confirmed the `FIXTURE_TRANSCRIPT` path regression on the move to `tests/golf/`; `git diff dev -- tests/golf/replay.test.ts` in worktree `wl-CG-0MUIH2ZZY0019MG2` confirmed the `a341ec3c` correction.

### Open questions

None remaining.

# Task: Create the nine public GitHub repositories and push dev plus seeded main

## Goal

As a distribution maintainer the nine repositories exist publicly on GitHub at
the remotes recorded in `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json`, each carrying the
extracted, history-preserving F9 `src/`-layout tree on `dev` and a `main` seeded
from it — the authorised publication that the F4 producer gate deferred.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The nine target names and remotes are resolved from
   `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` (no hard-coded repository names); all nine
   exist on GitHub under `TheWizardsCode` — `tableau-card-engine-core`,
   `tce-golf`, `tce-beleaguered-castle`, `tce-blackjack`, `tce-sushi-go`,
   `tce-feudalism`, `tce-lost-cities`, `tce-main-street`, `tce-coloretto` —
   verified with `gh api repos/TheWizardsCode/<name>` returning HTTP 200.
2. Every repository is **public** (`gh api ... --jq .visibility` prints
   `public`, matching parent Appendix Q1).
3. The published refs are exactly the agreed set: `dev` plus `main` seeded from
   `dev` (`main` default). `git ls-remote --heads` shows no `wl-*`/feature
   branches and `git ls-remote --tags` shows no monorepo `v0.1.x` tags
   (parent Appendix Q4).
4. Retained commit counts on the pushed `dev` match the C3 evidence, and the
   published trees are in the final layout: the core repo holds the engine + Gym
   + launcher shell and **no** `example-games/<game>`; each game repo has its
   source at repo-root `src/`.
5. Each game repo wires the engine as the `core` git submodule pointing at
   `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`; `.gitmodules`
   is present and `git submodule status` is clean after a fresh clone.
6. The source monorepo is unchanged (clean working tree, unchanged `dev` SHA)
   and nothing is pushed to the launcher repository's `main`.
7. Publication evidence — the per-repo retained commit counts and the source
   `dev` SHA — is recorded as a comment on the parent CG-0MUHK5NND0024J1S.

## Minimal Implementation

- Run the C2 helper in `--dry-run` first and confirm the plan matches
  `repo-layout.json` and the C3 evidence.
- Create and push only the agreed refs; seed `main` from `dev` once and leave
  the default branch set to `main`.
- Audit each remote immediately after pushing (`gh api`, `git ls-remote`) and
  record the evidence on the parent.
- Use SSH remotes throughout, consistent with the layout file.

**Key Files:**

- `scripts/configs/repo-layout.json` — authoritative names, slugs and remotes.
- `scripts/publish-repos.ts` — the C2 helper used to create and push.
- `docs/dev/repo-publication-decision.md` — the ref/safety contract applied.

**Dependencies:**

- **C2** — the publication helper (idempotency and safety guards).
- **C3** — the extracted and scaffolded local repos and their commit-count
  evidence.

**Deliverables:**

- Nine public GitHub repositories with the F9-layout history on `dev` and
  seeded `main`.
- Audit evidence recorded on the parent work item.

# Task: Verify fresh remote clones — game repos and launcher presets

## Goal

As a game developer, a fresh clone of a published game repo (with the engine
pulled in through the `core` submodule) installs, builds and unit-tests
successfully; and as a distribution builder the launcher can compose a subset of
the remote repos as siblings.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. In a clean temporary directory,
   `git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tce-golf.git`
   followed by `npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit`
   succeeds.
2. The same sequence succeeds for `tce-main-street` (parent AC3).
3. A fresh clone of `tableau-card-engine-core` succeeds and
   `npm install && npm run build && npm test -- --project unit` passes inside
   it.
4. The launcher composes a subset of the **remote** repos as siblings against
   fresh clones: `GAMES_CONFIG=solo` and `GAMES_CONFIG=full` builds
   (`npm run build`) both succeed (parent AC4).
5. The exact commands executed and their outcomes are recorded on the parent
   work item as verification evidence; any failure is triaged into a critical
   `test-failure` work item rather than worked around.

## Minimal Implementation

- Clone into a clean temp directory (never reuse a prior checkout) so the
  submodule resolution on clone is genuinely exercised.
- Run the clone/build/test sequence for golf and main-street, plus core.
- For the launcher presets, clone the remote game repos as siblings under the
  paths the presets reference (`../tce-<game>`) and build with `GAMES_CONFIG`
  set to `solo` then `full`.
- Record failures with the exact command and output before triaging.

**Key Files:**

- `configs/solo.json` — the one-game preset spot check.
- `configs/full.json` — the all-games preset spot check.
- `scripts/vite-game-discovery-plugin.ts` — sibling-repo discovery used by the
  presets.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — the documented clone/build/test workflow under test.

**Dependencies:**

**C4** (the repositories must exist and be pushed before a fresh clone can be
verified).

**Deliverables:**

- Fresh-clone verification evidence for golf, main-street, core and the
  `solo`/`full` launcher presets, recorded on the parent.

**C4 evidence: the nine repositories are created and published (CG-0MUIND9RO001WKNO)**

All nine repositories now exist on GitHub under `TheWizardsCode`, are **public**, and publish exactly `dev` + `main` with **`main` as the default branch** and **no tags**. Verified with `gh api repos/.../.jq visibility/default_branch` and `git ls-remote --heads/--tags`.

| repo | visibility/default | heads | tags | published `dev` commits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| tableau-card-engine-core | public/main | dev, main | 0 | 806 |
| tce-golf | public/main | dev, main | 0 | 217 |
| tce-beleaguered-castle | public/main | dev, main | 0 | 197 |
| tce-blackjack | public/main | dev, main | 0 | 26 |
| tce-sushi-go | public/main | dev, main | 0 | 140 |
| tce-feudalism | public/main | dev, main | 0 | 126 |
| tce-lost-cities | public/main | dev, main | 0 | 167 |
| tce-main-street | public/main | dev, main | 0 | 1050 |
| tce-coloretto | public/main | dev, main | 0 | 41 |

**Layout verified on the remotes:** core `example-games/` contains only `gym` (no games); each game repo has repo-root `src/` (`src/scenes/...`), a `.gitmodules` and a `core` git submodule pointing at `git@github.com:TheWizardsCode/tableau-card-engine-core.git`. Core `main` = `2e9fc0e5`; game `main` == `dev` at their seeded tip.

**Source revision:** the published trees are the C3 extraction from monorepo `dev` `b6ce40e5` plus the C3 fix commit `76e600f9` (used as the local verification source). The monorepo `dev` has since advanced to `44ea9126` (C1/C2 + concurrent fixes); the ship process keeps the remotes current. The source monorepo working tree stayed clean and its `dev` SHA was never rewritten (extraction operated on clones; the launcher repository's `main` was not pushed to).

**Count delta vs C3 evidence (AC4):** each count is C3's + 1, because publishing required one new commit on top of the extracted history — the scaffold commit for the eight game repos (`chore: scaffold single-game launcher …`) and a `.gitignore` commit for core. The retained *extraction* content still matches C3; the +1 is the publication overlay, not a re-extraction.

**Publication mechanism:** `npm run publish:repos -- --repos-dir /home/rgardler/projects/tce-repos-f9` (C2 helper). Re-running it proved idempotency: core and golf reported `create: no (exists)` / `push: nothing (up to date)`, all others created+pushed, exit 0. No `--force`, no tags, no branch outside `{dev, main}`.

**Deviation recorded:** the F4/F9 scaffold defaults to a *sibling* core reference (`../tableau-card-engine-core`), which does not build under `git clone --recurse-submodules` (the submodule is at `./core`). The game repos were therefore re-scaffolded with `--core-rel ./core`, so `vite.config.ts`/`tsconfig.json` aliases and the shared-asset links resolve through the `core/` submodule. Built/unit-tested locally after the change for golf (tsc + build + 217 unit) and main-street (tsc + build + 3911 unit). C5 performs the authoritative fresh-clone verification.
